observations:
Torah #214 contains exactly one bechina: תַּלְמוּד ↔ לִילִית (gematria=480). This yields a single two-node package. No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate from this package.

The Torah's argument is a minimal two-part structure:
  Stage 1 — The bechina identity [Package 1: neutral]: תַּלְמוּד = לִילִית (gematria identity reveals structural kinship)
  Stage 2 — The eitza consequence: לִמּוּד כַּהֹגֶן → הַכְנָעָה / לִמּוּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי → כֹּחַ לִילִית

The good/evil mirror structure is present but it is entirely internal to Package 1. The Rebbe does not develop a separate evil package — the evil mirror of תַּלְמוּד is לִילִית herself, and they are already joined in the same package as two faces of the same gematria-reality. The single package spans both polarities simultaneously, which is structurally unusual and is the entire point of the Torah: the same Talmud that can liberate can also destroy, depending on the quality of learning.

No secondary clusters of bechina-related concepts were found in the source text. The following concepts appear only in eitza contexts and do not warrant new packages: בַּעַל דָּבָר (adversary — referenced narratively), לִמּוּד כַּהֹגֶן (proper learning — an eitza condition), לִמּוּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי (improper learning — an eitza condition), גְּמָרָא (Gemara — a specification of תַּלְמוּד, not an independent bechina node).

Conclusion: Torah #214 is structurally complete with a single neutral package of two nodes united by gematria-bechina. Its teaching is entirely carried by one bechina identity and one branching eitza consequence. No new packages are needed or warranted.
